subject: MapleHealth pool provisioning sprint — operational handshake and regional selection
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <ops@maplehealth.com>
Date: 2029-06-04T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: MapleHealth: pool provisioning sprint - kickoff and constraints

Team / Alex,

Thanks for the kickoff earlier — putting the initial checklist here so we have a single source before the sprint starts next week. High-level asks from MapleHealth that we need to validate before we turn up the reserved pool:

- Expected baseline QPS: 450 req/min (spiky at 2.5x during 09:00–11:00 PT)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 220ms for text-generation endpoints (50-token avg)
- Data residency: US-only; keys must integrate with customer KMS (Tina on cc)
- Integration touchpoints: network CIDR, egress rules, and service-account provisioning

Attachments: sprint_backlog.xlsx (work items), network_diagram.pdf (their VPC sketch)

Immediate asks for Redwood: please confirm preferred region (us-west1 vs us-east4) and recommended min pool size to meet the above SLOs. Karthik — can you sketch an autoscale/burst suggestion we can surface to procurement?

Priyom
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <ops@maplehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Tina Gomez <tina@maplehealth.com>
Date: 2029-06-04T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MapleHealth: pool provisioning sprint - kickoff and constraints

Thanks, Priyom. Quick notes from platform and ops perspective: 

- Region: for US-only residency and lower egress latency to your users in the West, we recommend us-west1 as primary with us-east4 as hot-failover. That keeps replication and cross-region egress minimal.
- Min pool sizing: to hold p95 < 220ms at baseline plus 2.5x spikes, recommend an initial reserved pool sized at ~8 A100-equivalent slots with a burst policy allowing +50% on demand for short spikes (3–5 minutes).
- Autoscale triggers: CPU/GPU utilization > 65% sustained for 45s, queue depth > 40 requests for 30s. Warm-up policy: keep a 2-instance warm pool for cold-start-sensitive routes.

Questions for MapleHealth (Alex/Tina):
1) Are you comfortable with A100-equivalent capacity? If you plan to use quantized models we can reduce slot sizing but need early heads-up.
2) KMS: do you have a particular HSM or cloud-KMS instance for cross-account binding?

I'll draft a short mutual-action table and owners after we confirm those two items.

—Olga
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <ops@maplehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tina Gomez <tina@maplehealth.com>, procurement@maplehealth.com
Date: 2029-06-04T13:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MapleHealth: pool provisioning sprint - kickoff and constraints

On Tue, 4 Jun 2029 at 10:07, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Priyom. Quick notes from platform and ops perspective:

Thanks — us-west1 primary works. A few clarifications from our side:

- We will be running two model variants (clinical-instruct / clinical-instruct-quant). The quantized variant is preferred for cost but we want parity checks before we route traffic.
- KMS: we manage keys in AWS KMS; we can provide a cross-account role for Redwood to use envelope-encryption. Tina will follow up with KMS ARN.
- Procurement: to enable burst we need a straight-commit schedule in the SOW. Can Redwood outline a short burst pricing appendix we can include? procurement@maplehealth.com

We attached a short network constraints doc in the Drive link (see related_links).

—Alex
Senior Cloud Ops, MapleHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <ops@maplehealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Tina Gomez <tina@maplehealth.com>
Date: 2029-06-05T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MapleHealth: pool provisioning sprint - kickoff and constraints

Thanks Alex — noted on KMS and quantized variant. Proposed technical handoff / canary plan below (short):

- Week 0 (pre-sprint): exchange service account, VPC peering checklist, CIDR validation (Network owner: MapleHealth)
- Week 1 (canary): provision a 3-slot canary pool in us-west1 running clinical-instruct-quant with traffic routed at 5% using weighted routing. Run parity tests (latency and output quality) against production-like prompt set. Canary runbook: canary-runbook.md (attached).
- Week 2 (turn-up): scale reserved pool to 8 slots; apply burst policy: +4 ephemeral slots (50%) with burst window 5m and cooldown 3m. Autoscale thresholds as noted by Olga.
- Fallback: if quantized variant shows >5% quality regression vs baseline, automatic fallback to non-quantized variant for 25% of requests and rollback canary.

I'll own the canary and runbook execution. Monica — can you own procurement cadence and the burst-pricing appendix? Priyom / Olga — we should align on exact SLO language for the SOW.

Thanks,
Karthik
Software Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MapleHealth: pool provisioning sprint - kickoff and constraints — mutual action plan

Alex / Tina / Procurement,

Appreciate the confirmations. I put together a short mutual-action plan below — please reply with owner confirmations and any date conflicts. If we get alignment by EOD Friday (2029-06-07) we can start the canary on Monday 2029-06-10.

Mutual action plan (owners / target dates):
- Network & IAM exchange: MapleHealth (Alex) — complete by 2029-06-07
- KMS ARN + cross-account role: MapleHealth (Tina) — complete by 2029-06-07
- Procurement: burst pricing appendix & SOW addendum: MapleHealth procurement + Monica Patel (Redwood) — draft by 2029-06-07, finalize by 2029-06-09
- Canary provisioning & parity tests: Karthik (Redwood) — run 2029-06-10 to 2029-06-12
- Decision gate (go/no-go for full turn-up): Joint review 2029-06-13

Notes / expectations:
- Autoscale / burst settings: initial reserved 8 slots (A100-equivalent) + burst +4 ephemeral slots; burst billing will be meter-based with the appendix limiting burst minutes per month and clear overage terms.
- Quality guardrails: parity tests must pass (<=5% regression on our test set) before we route >25% traffic to quantized model.

Attachments referenced: sprint_backlog.xlsx, network_diagram.pdf, canary-runbook.md

If that looks good I'll convert this into a short Drive checklist and update the HubSpot deal (link below). Please reply with owner confirmations.

Olga Petrov
